run.question:
I'm connected to the ci-cd cluster. We got a P1 alert and need help finding the root cause.
Our cluster inventory is in the app-235-cluster-inventory index and deployment/change history
is in the app-235-change-history index. Please search these indices to investigate.
[
  {
    "annotations": {
      "description": "Online Devices count gradual decrease over 8 hours in [clientorg-alpha] [56%] for over 30m",
      "workload": "clientorg-alpha"
    },
    "fingerprint": "xx1234567890abcd",
    "labels": {
      "alertname": "onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease",
      "app": "lambda-dashboard-monitoring",
      "cluster": "us-prod-eks",
      "grafana_dashboard_name": "Production-Performance-Overview",
      "org": "clientorg-alpha",
      "severity": "critical",
      "slack_channel": "sre-alerts-channel"
    },
    "startsAt": "30 minutes ago",
    "status": "firing"
  }
]
The alert started right after a deployment. Can you check what's the root cause?

report.summary: The alert (onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease, app lambda-dashboard-monitoring, cluster us-prod-eks, org/workload clientorg-alpha, severity critical) does not describe anything observable in the environment this Run could reach. The connected cluster's namespace list contains app-282, default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo, with no clientorg-alpha, no ci and no lambda-dashboard-monitoring workload. The change-history index returned exactly three changes inside the authorized window, all for cluster ci-cd in namespace ci: jenkins 2.426.2-lts to 2.426.3-lts at 2026-11-20T23:25:09Z, argocd-server v2.9.2 to v2.9.3 at 2026-11-21T00:25:09Z and a gitlab-runner scale from 2 to 3 replicas at 2026-11-21T03:25:09Z; the inventory shows those three Running with 1, 2 and 3 replicas. None of them is the alerting application, and the newest recorded change (03:25:09Z) precedes the alert's approximate start (~04:55:22Z, derived from the relative text '30 minutes ago') by about 1.5 hours, so the premise that the alert started right after a deployment is not supported by the retrieved change records. Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable for the whole Run, so no error-rate, latency, alert-rule or trace check exists for any service. Root cause cannot be named: the alerting cluster, org and application are absent from the evidence and no object is shown applying a fault. In the connected cluster 26 deployments reported Available=True and Progressing=True at query time, and no error-matching log line was returned for two otel-demo pods, but neither observation ties to the alerting workload.

claims.text: The change-history index returned exactly three change records inside the authorized window, all for cluster ci-cd in namespace ci: BUILD-7X4Q9M jenkins 2.426.2-lts to 2.426.3-lts at 2026-11-20T23:25:09Z; BUILD-3NR8Y1 argocd-server v2.9.2 to v2.9.3 (ArgoCD security patch update) at 2026-11-21T00:25:09Z; BUILD-5PW2K6 gitlab-runner scaled from 2 to 3 replicas at 2026-11-21T03:25:09Z. The newest of these is the gitlab-runner scale at 2026-11-21T03:25:09Z.

The cluster-inventory index returned the matching workloads for cluster ci-cd, namespace ci: gitlab-runner with 3 replicas (gitlab/gitlab-runner:v16.7.0), jenkins with 1 replica (jenkins/jenkins:2.426.3-lts) and argocd-server with 2 replicas (quay.io/argoproj/argocd:v2.9.3), each reported status Running.

The connected cluster's namespace list returned app-282, default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo; it contains no namespace named clientorg-alpha and no namespace named ci.

The cluster-wide deployment read returned 26 deployments, each with status conditions Available=True and Progressing=True and with ready and available replicas equal to the desired replica count (for example otel-demo/frontend, otel-demo/checkout, otel-demo/payment, kube-system/coredns and app-282/checkout); no deployment in that list was short of ready replicas at query time.

The hypothesis that a recorded deployment of the alerting application lambda-dashboard-monitoring immediately preceded the alert is not supported: the only deployment or scale records inside the authorized window are the three ci-cd changes to jenkins, argocd-server and gitlab-runner, and the latest of them (2026-11-21T03:25:09Z) is roughly 1.5 hours before the alert's approximate start.

The otel-demo flagd-config ConfigMap (key demo.flagd.json) defines 11 fault-style flags (productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad), and every one of them has defaultVariant set to "off" while state is ENABLED; no flag in that configuration is switched on.

One deployment read returned an app-102b/traffic-manager deployment with 3 desired replicas, no readyReplicas and no availableReplicas, image nginx:latest, and the grouped event read returned app-102b events: 1 Deployment ScalingReplicaSet, 3 ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate and 3 each of Pod Created, Scheduled, Pulled, Pulling and Started.

Pods checkout-698c8f5df-dwqgn and loki-66445c6d6f-fldxz in namespace app-282 were created at 2026-11-21T05:25:52Z, owned by ReplicaSets checkout-698c8f5df and loki-66445c6d6f, became Ready, and had restartCount 0; this is after the authorized window's end (2026-11-21T05:25:22Z).

Because the alert's cluster (us-prod-eks), org/workload (clientorg-alpha) and application (lambda-dashboard-monitoring) appear in none of the reachable objects or records, the failing workload most likely lives in a cluster other than the connected one, and its metrics, logs, deployment records and change history are outside this Run's reach; the alert annotation also describes a gradual 8-hour decline, which does not by itself fit a single deployment event, though the underlying online-device series could not be read to test this.

Obtain telemetry from the cluster the alert names (us-prod-eks): the deployment/change history and the online-device count series for clientorg-alpha/lambda-dashboard-monitoring around the alert start, before attributing the P1 to any Kubernetes object in the ci-cd environment.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable for the entire Run: get_metric_names, get_label_values, execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_prometheus_target and list_prometheus_rules each returned status error with reason SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error-rate, latency, up-ness or alerting-rule reading exists for any service, and the state of the rule onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease is unknown.
Jaeger was unreachable for the entire Run: traces_list_services and traces_search both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no service error spans or call chains could be checked.
change_history is listed as a not-integrated source; only the Elasticsearch index app-235-change-history could be used and no other deployment-record source was available.
The alert's startsAt is the relative text '30 minutes ago'; the exact start instant is unknown and an approximate 2026-11-21T04:55:22Z (window end minus 30 minutes) was assumed when comparing times.

The change-history search filtered to timestamp and returned nothing (status no_data) for the window 2026-11-21T04:25:22Z to 2026-11-21T05:25:22Z, and a targeted search for cluster=us-prod-eks, app_name=lambda-dashboard-monitoring or namespace=clientorg-alpha returned nothing (status no_data) in both app-235-change-history and app-235-cluster-inventory; these empty results only show those queries matched nothing, not that the entities are absent.

Four documents in the two indices lie outside the authorized window (1 of 4 change-history documents and 3 of 6 inventory documents) and could not be read, because the time filter on timestamp/last_updated cannot be disabled; their content is unknown.

No metric name or label value for an online-device count, lambda-dashboard-monitoring or clientorg-alpha could be enumerated because the Prometheus discovery tools were unavailable; those signals are unchecked, not shown to be absent.

The cluster reads were internally inconsistent: one deployment read returned app-102b/traffic-manager (3 desired, 0 ready) and the event read returned app-102b pod-creation events around 2026-11-21T05:23:29-05:23:31Z, but later reads of the same target returned 8 namespaces without app-102b, 26 deployments without traffic-manager, and queries scoped to namespace app-102b returned nothing (status no_data); the existence and state of app-102b could not be confirmed and it has no identified relation to the alerting application.

Pod-log error queries returned no matching lines for otel-demo/frontend-6c9bc688bf-58jmw and otel-demo/checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n inside the window (status no_data; checkout read 273 lines, none matched err|error|fail|exception|panic|timeout|refused); this does not prove those services were healthy nor connect them to the alert, and other otel-demo service logs were not read.
The trigger and change record for the app-282 checkout/loki rollout that created pods at 2026-11-21T05:25:52Z are unknown; it lies after the window end and is not tied to the alert.
next_steps: Pull the deployment/change feed and the online-device metric series for cluster us-prod-eks, org clientorg-alpha, app lambda-dashboard-monitoring, and compare the 8-hour decline against any deployment timestamp there.

Re-run Prometheus and Jaeger checks (error rates, latencies, error spans, alert-rule state) once those sources are reachable, to determine whether any service in the connected cluster was failing during 04:00-05:25Z.
Ask the alert owner for an absolute startsAt and the Grafana dashboard/rule definition for onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease so the alerting signal's deviation point can be established.
Verify whether app-102b and its traffic-manager deployment exist, and if so whether they are related to the alert, given the contradictory cluster reads observed here.
